stem: A commonly taught minimum fixative-to-tissue volume is:
rationale: A generous fixative volume, often around 10:1, helps prevent depletion and dilution.

distractor_rationales.A: A 1:10 ratio reverses the intended relationship and provides too little fixative for the tissue volume.
distractor_rationales.B: A 1:1 ratio is generally inadequate because tissue can deplete or dilute the fixative.
distractor_rationales.D: A 100:1 ratio may be used in special circumstances but is not the commonly taught routine minimum for every specimen.

learning_objective: Recall the commonly taught approximate fixative-to-tissue volume used for routine fixation.
